case_name: R. N. Goyal v Ashwani Kumar Gupta and Others
facts: The Order of the Court was as follows:...

In the Directorate of Industries in the State of Haryana, there is a service known as 'Group A' Service (hereinafter referred to as 'the Service') and the members of the Service are governed by the Rules, known as 'the Haryana Industries (Group A) Service Rules, 1986' (for short 'the Rules').
The respondents herein challenged the appointment of the appellant by means of a petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
It is not disputed that at the relevant time the appellant was working as the Deputy Director (Engineering Goods).
It is further not disputed that the appellant did not have the qualification of five years' experience as Deputy Director (Technical), Technical Specialist for Plastic Goods.
issues: What are the requisite qualifications for appointment to the post of Technical Expert (Mechanical Engineering)?
petitioner_arguments: The Rules framed under Article 309 of the Constitution, if it is for general good, causes hardship to an individual, the same could not be a ground for striking down the Rules.
court_reasoning: A perusal of the aforesaid Rule 9(1)(b) shows that only those Deputy Directors, who are either Technical or Technical Specialists for Plastic Goods or Deputy Directors (Industries) having requisite qualification are eligible for appointment to the post of Technical Expert.

For the aforesaid reason, we are in agreement with the view taken by the High Court that the appellant did not possess the requisite qualification for being appointed as the Technical Expert (Mechanical Engineering).

We do not find any merit in the submission where the Rules framed under Article 309 of the Constitution, if it is for general good, causes hardship to an individual, the same could not be a ground for striking down the Rules.
holding: The appeals and writ petition are, accordingly, dismissed. There shall be no order as to costs.
The appeal is dismissed as not pressed.
cases_cited: R. N. Goyal v Ashwani Kumar Gupta
